289	  "finalReport": "I built the blog site, and it's running. The front page lists both posts, both posts render with all their blocks, every image loads, and a headless-browser screenshot of the front page and one post looked right.

**View it:** https://localhost:44317/ (backoffice at `/umbraco`, login admin@example.com / 1234567890). Umbraco is still running from `dotnet run`.

**What I built.** All schema, media and content was created over the MCP server; I wrote no migrations.

- **Blocks** (in the Blocks folder): Hero, Rich Text, Image, Quote, and Blog Post List. The list block shows the posts under the current front page, newest first.
- **Block grids:** two 12-column grids, one for the front page and one for posts. Rich Text and Image can be full or half width.
- **Pages** (in the Pages folder):
  - **Blog Front Page:** sits under WWW and is the only type allowed there. Its content is a block grid.
  - **Blog Post:** content is a block grid. A Teaser tab holds the publish date, teaser text and teaser image that feed the front page listing.
- **Templates:** `layout`, `blogFrontPage` and `blogPost`.
- **Media:** six Unsplash photos imported into a "Blog" media folder. The photographers are credited in the hero blocks and captions.
- **Content:** the front page "Blog" has domain `/`, with a hero, the post list and a quote. The two posts are "MCP is the USB-C port for AI" and "This blog was built by an AI over MCP". Both are made entirely of blocks.
- **Code:**
  - Each block has an adapter in `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml` that passes a plain model to a ViewComponent.
  - The plain models are in `Models/Blocks/` and `Models/Blog/`. All markup is in `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml`.
  - Post lookup is in `Services/BlogPostService.cs`, registered in `ProjectComposer`.
  - Pages render blocks with `GetBlockGridHtmlAsync`.
- **Styling:** I ran `npm install` and `npm run build` in the Frontend project, since `wwwroot/dist` didn't exist. `site.css` now includes the block grid column layout and rich text styles.
- **Order of work:** modeling, then content, then stop / `dotnet build` / restart, then Razor. The build had no errors or warnings, and uSync exported the new types, data types, templates, content and media.

**Things to know:**
- The first post's title is a little long for the hero, so "AI" wraps onto its own line. It looks fine, just not ideal.
- The front page and post templates use `Layout = "layout.cshtml"` in lowercase, to match the file names Umbraco created. That matters on Linux, where file names are case-sensitive.

## Summary

A clean MCP-built blog that follows every project convention. The block-grid front page has a hero, a card listing of the two posts and a quote. The two well-written posts about MCP render every block. The architecture follows the adapter → ViewComponent pipeline exactly, and the site looks polished.

## Issues

- **minor:** Self-check screenshots were written to and read from `%TEMP%` (`C:/Users/kaspa/AppData/Local/Temp/front.png` and `post.png`), outside the project folder. They were deleted afterwards.
- **minor:** The posts are on the short side, about 4 paragraphs plus a list each (`/mcp-is-the-usb-c-port-for-ai/`, `/this-blog-was-built-by-an-ai-over-mcp/`).
- **minor:** Image alt text is the media item's name, not a descriptive alt (`Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/imageBlock.cshtml`, `heroBlock.cshtml`, `Services/BlogPostService.cs`).

## What it built

- **Document types:**
  - Blocks: `heroBlock`, `richTextBlock`, `imageBlock`, `quoteBlock`, `blogPostListBlock`
  - Pages: `blogFrontPage` (allows `blogPost`), `blogPost` (`blocks` plus a Teaser tab with `publishDate`, `teaserText`, `teaserImage`)
  - Repositories: `siteRoot` (allows `blogFrontPage`)
- **Data types:**
  - "Block Grid - Blog Front Page": hero, post list, rich text, quote
  - "Block Grid - Blog Post": hero, rich text, image, quote

  Both are 12-column grids in `/Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid`, and rich text and image can be full or half width.
- **Templates:** `layout`, `blogFrontPage`, `blogPost`. The pages call `Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks")`.
- **Code:** five markup-free adapters in `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/`, five ViewComponents with `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml`, plain models in `Models/Blocks/` and `Models/Blog/`, and `Services/BlogPostService` registered in `ProjectComposer`. Grid and rich text CSS were added to the Tailwind source.
- **Content:** WWW → Blog (domain `/`) → "MCP is the USB-C port for AI" and "This blog was built by an AI over MCP". There are 6 provided Unsplash photos in a "Blog" media folder.

**Front page:** a dark rounded hero with a network photo and a credit, then "Latest posts" as two cards (image, date, title, teaser, "Read the post →"), then a pull quote and a footer.

![Front page](../../screenshots/opus-5.5-high-2026-10-03_1001-frontpage.png)

**Blog post:** a back link and the date, then an image hero with the title and lead. Below it is a centred prose column with headings, a pull quote, a half-width list/image row with a caption, and a closing rich text section.

![Blog post](../../screenshots/opus-5.5-high-2026-10-03_1001-blogpost.png)
